minutes.headline: Select Board backed a senior bag-relief pilot in principle but put the bag fee decision off to next week
minutes.summary: The board ratified two seasonal lifeguard appointments, reviewed the draft RFP for old primary school landscape architecture services, and heard about a MassHousing 40B site approval request for Pond View Commons. It rescinded the pandemic-era vote letting the chair sign warrants alone and approved two sets of minutes. Most discussion was the pay-as-you-throw bag fee increase and a senior bag relief pilot, deferred to next week to gather public input. The board then went into executive session on the town manager contract.

what_happened.line: The Select Board put off a decision on the pay-as-you-throw bag fee increase and a senior bag relief pilot until next week, to take public input first.
The board voted unanimously to rescind the pandemic-era vote letting the chair or vice chair sign warrants alone on the board's behalf.
The board ratified two seasonal lifeguard appointments, all in favor.
Members thought the draft RFP for old primary school landscape architecture is too broad for the town meeting appropriation and may need phasing; feedback goes to the town manager.
The board heard about a MassHousing site approval request under Chapter 40B for Pond View Commons, then moved to executive session on the town manager contract.

why_it_matters: The bag fee is a per-household cost: the board is weighing a smaller increase paid from surplus against a larger one, and a member said that surplus will be used up, so a further increase next year is likely.
The old primary school RFP sets how far the town's design money can go, so a broad scope could mean the work is phased across more than one appropriation vote.
watch_next: The board's next-week agenda: the bag fee, the senior relief pilot, and a vote on board goals.
The finalized old primary school landscape architecture RFP, which the board aims to complete next week.
